description.narrative: Project Goal: The health of aquatic ecosystems restored, cooperation and regional integration improved through enhancing the contribution of the Blue Economy. Project Objectives: 1) To establish functional BE structure at regional and national levels to cater for the regional and national needs (selected member states of IGAD) 2) To assess the impact of pollution and develop mitigation measures on aquatic biodiversity and ecosystems 3) To enhance capacity in knowledge generation and dissemination on key BE questions for the IGAD region for learning, policy and practice change among the Member States.

IGAD (Intergovernmental Authority on Development) har till Sida ansökt om medel för att implementera insatsen "Intensifiering av den blåa ekonomin i IGAD´s kustmedlemsländer för stärkande av biologisk mångfald och för diversifierade försörjningsmöjligheter". Insatsen ska bidraga till att anpassa IGAD´s strategi för Blå ekonomi. Strategin utvecklades år 2020 och inväntar godkännande av medlemssstaterna. Denna process utgör en del av insatsen. Insatsens övergripande mål är att restaurera de akvatiska ekosystemens häsostatus samt förbättra samarbetet och den regionala integrationen genom att bidraga till att utveckla den blåa ekonomin i regionen.
Specifika mål är: a) att etablera funktionella strukturer för en blå ekonomi på regional och nationell nivå b) att tillgodose regionala och nationella behov (hos utvalda IGAD- stater) b) att bedöma påverkansgraden av föroreningarna och att vidtaga åtgärder för att begränsa miljöföroreningarnas påverkan på den akvatiska biologiska mångfalden och ekosystemen och c) att öka kapaciteten samt generera och sprida kunskap inom centrala frågeställningar för IGAD regionen för lärande, policy och praxis bland medlemsstaterna.
Insatsen kommer att genomföras under en treårs-period från juli 2021 till och med juni 2024 och den totala kostnaden för Sida är 42 miljoner SEK.
IGAD kommer att samarbeta med den svenska Havs- och Vattenmyndigheten (HaV) för kunskapsöverföring och genomförande av utbildningar.

The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) has applied to Sida for a support to implement their project entitled Enhancing Blue Economy in the IGAD Coastal Member States for Biodiversity Conservations and Livelihood Diversification. This project will contribute to the adoption of an IGAD Blue Economy Strategy that was developed in 2020 and is awaiting approval by Member States the process of which is part of the project. The overall objective of the project is to restore the health of aquatic ecosystems, improve cooperation and regional integration through enhancing the contribution of the Blue Economy.
The Specific Objectives are: a) to establish functional Blue Economy structure at regional and national levels a) to cater for the regional and national needs (selected member states of IGAD); b) to assess the impact of pollution and develop mitigation measures on aquatic biodiversity and ecosystems; and c) to enhance capacity in knowledge generation and dissemination on key Blue Economy questions for the IGAD region for learning, policy and practice change among the Member States.
The project will be implemented in Sudan, Djibouti, Somalia and Kenya over a period of three years from June 2021 to May 2024 with a total cost of SEK 42 Million to be contributed by Sida.
IGAD will partner with the Swedish Agency for Marine and Water Management (SwAM) for knowledge transfer and provision of trainings.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between Sida and IGAD

description.narrative:
The African Union has identified Blue Economy (BE) development as a priority goal towards achieving the aspiration on A prosperous Africa based on inclusive growth and sustainable development within the context of the Africa Union Agenda 2063. In line with this ambitious plan the IGAD region has huge Blue Economy potential to contribute. The four coastal member states of IGAD (Djibouti, Kenya, Somalia, and Sudan) have an aggregated Exclusive Economic Zones of more than one million Km2 area and about 5, 000 km of coastline. To utilize the Blue Economy (BE) potential of the region sustainably, IGAD has developed a five-year Blue Economy strategy (2021 2025) and Implementation Plan (BESIP), aligned with Africans Blue Economy Strategy, with a vision of developing an inclusive and sustainable Blue Economy that significantly contributes to the Horn of Africans transformation. The IGAD Blue Economy Strategy and Implementation Plan intend to structure the Blue Economy implementation at both national and regional levels while increasing cooperation and regional integration and strengthening support to the member states to effectively translate policies into concrete actions.
As the contribution is in its last year of the implementation period, the partner has submitted a more consolidated narrative and financial reports covering the hole life period of the project. The reports clearly indicated that the project has achieved most of the results as planned. However, mainly due to COVID restrictions which has delayed the project staff recruitment, the region peace and security issues as well as the severe drought, desert locust invasion and flooding, shifted the priority activities towards emergencies.
The key project achievements during the life span of the contribution are summarized below. The IGAD five year (2021 2025) Blue Economy Strategy has been adopted and the Declaration has been signed by Ministers of IGAD MSs in charge of coordination of BE. Lead institution in charge of coordinating BE sectors in each IGAD Member States (MSs) identified and functioning as a focal institution. IGAD region BE Coordination Platform (IBECP), a technical working group (TWG), established. All national focal persons (NFPs) of the IGAD BE Project are members of the regional Blue Economy Platform (IBECP).
In all the 7 IGAD Member States, national BE baseline study conducted and reported. These BE baseline reports will serve as the main background document to prepare national BE strategies for each member states. National Blue Economy Strategy of each MS has been developed and endorsed by all the seven IGAD Member States.
As part of media campaigns and digital advocacy programmes journalists selected and trained in each IGAD MS to report BE issues BE National Focal Person (NFP) has been selected in each IGAD MS to comprehend and practice digital advocacy for development projects, to formulate messages convincing targeted audiences and to assign roles and responsibilities among the stakeholders to step in the campaign planning.
National BE Coordination Platform (NBECP) led by the NFP in the respective IGAD member states. Gender analysis study of BE in the IGAD Coastal MSs conducted, and gender responsive action plan developed and implemented. IGAD has been selected as lead REC on Blue Economy by AUC to lead women and BE Chapter of the same. The Project Technical Working Group (TWG) and Steering Committee meetings have been conducted on a regular basis to guide the implementation of the project activities and review project progresses and activity plans. Some of the planned project activities has been delayed due to external factors such as COVID19 restrictions which has delayed the project staff recruitment, the region peace and security issues as well as the severe drought, desert locust invasion and flooding, which has shifted the priority activities towards emergencies in the first two years of project implementation period. As a result of this, the partner has requested a one year No Cost Extension to enable accomplish all the remaining activities and facilitate smooth closure and project reporting. Accordingly, Sida has accepted the request and formally sent no objection letter confirming the extension of the project implementation period to be until 30 June 2025.
The extension period will support the completion of the following key activities: Consolidate the coordination and institutionalization of Blue Economy at region and Member States level, developing a regional framework for plastic pollution management, rehabilitation of Siesta Beach as pilot demonstration site for healthy interaction between human and seascape, consolidate knowledge sharing and documentation and Final project evaluation to ensure sustainability. Hence the decision to give a one-year no cost extension by Sida would increase the chances that the project objectives will be achieved. It was also assessed that there have been no significant changes observed in the context in which the contribution is implemented, making the Theory of Change (ToC) still relevant and applicable. Hence it is likely that the objectives of the project will be achieved by the end of the project period given the overall identified risks reduced.
Overall, the IGAD Blue Economy team has done a great job in supporting member states to develop their blue economy strategy, to validate and endorsed them. IGAD also coordinated with AU-IBAR and ECoFish to organize knowledge fair on Blue Economy during the reporting period. Moreover, IGAD has strengthened its partnership with the Swedish Agency for Marine and Water Management (SwAM); and has created the opportunity for Member States of IGAD to learn from the experiences of the agency.
